previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a complex history including fibrosing mesenteritis, recurrent small bowel obstruction, and G-tube dependence, was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea concerning for partial small bowel obstruction. She was managed conservatively with NPO status, G-tube suction, and pain control. Due to prolonged inability to eat, TPN was initiated and arranged for home continuation. Her G-tube was replaced due to granulation tissue, and her warfarin dose was adjusted to 5 mg daily with a therapeutic INR at discharge. She experienced somnolence from increased narcotics and antiemetics, prompting a return to her baseline medication regimen. Her condition improved, and she was discharged home with home health services for TPN and close outpatient follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ yo F with mesenteric fibromyotosis, chronic 
abdominal pain and recurrent small bowel obstructions admitted 
with obstructive symptoms. She was found to have a patent bowels 
on small bowel follow-though with compression as the site of a 
presumed adhesion (adhesion was visualized on a previous CT 
scan). While in the hospital, she developed a Port-a-cath 
associated coag negative staph line infection and bacteremia.

Management by problem outlined below:
*Abdominal pain, nausea. This is a chronic, recurrent issue 
resulting in numerous prolonged hospitalizations. She was 
managed conservatively, NPO, IV fluids, G-tube to suction on IV 
morphine PCA with IV anti-emetics as well as ongoing use of 
misoprostol and octreotide as per her outpatient GI regimen. Due 
to poor progress and chronic malnutrition she was started on 
TPN. 

She underwent a Gastrografin study on ___ to check the tube 
patency due to increased drainage around the tube, and her G 
tube was changed out on ___. An EGD was done on ___ and showed 
no obstruction but was somewhat limited by her post-surgical 
anatomy. A KUB from ___ showed no evidence of obstruction. She 
was evaluated by surgery who did not feel that she warranted a 
surgery at this time given no clear evidence of obstruction and 
her history of multiple surgeries in the past. She also received 
methylnaltrexone for a concomitant presumed functional bowel 
problem. She was also seen by the chronic pain service and was 
started on amitriptyline. She had a very slow recovery with 
difficulty weaning from IV narcotics, but was eventually weaned 
to a regimen of oral concentrated morphine at similar dose prior 
to admission.  

*Coag negative staph line infection and bacteremia
The patient developed fevers up to 101 and was found on both 
peripheral blood cultures and those drawn off of her port-a-cath 
to have coag negative staph growth She was seen by the ID 
consult team and will be treated with 2 weeks of systemic 
vancomycin therapy and vancomycin lock therapy on her 
port-a-cath, as organism was MRSE (not MRSA) and TEE negative.  
Antibiotic therapy concluded on ___, and she will need weekly 
surveillance cultures through her primary MD for two weeks 
following this. Her first surveillance culture was drawn on ___ 
and she will need a repeat culture drawn on ___. 

*DVT--The patient has a history of DVT and her INR was 
sub-therapeutic - possibly because of vitamin K in the TPN and 
possibly because of poor absorption. Her Coumadin dose was 
up-titrated to a max of 12.5mg daily without any INR response. 
Given her history of difficulty with supra-therapeutic INR's it 
seemed unsafe to continue this escalated dose (from her usual 
dose of 5mg daily) because sometime in the future she may begin 
absorbing this better or come off of TPN and develop dangerous 
elevations in INR. Therefore, she was switched to ___ for 
systemic anticoagulation and continued on this at discharge.

*Hypotension. The patient was noted to be hypotensive on ___ 
although she was asymptomatic. A cortisol level was sent and the 
7 am level was 3.7. A ___ stim was performed and at 0, 30 and 
60 minutes the levels were 24, 6.6. and 29.4 respectively. It is 
likely that one of these samples may have been switched since 
cosyntropin was given after time point 0. In either case, given 
these cortisol levels in the ___, she was felt to not have 
adrenal insufficiency. Her low blood pressure resolved and was 
likely due to increased ostomy output relative to her intake.

*Nausea. The patient has numerous allergies to medications. She 
tolerated the IV antiemetic here that she has taken in liquid 
form at home, Phenergan. On discharge, she should be 
transitioned back to the liquid form of the medication. Her 
Reglan was stopped during this admission as it was not working 
and there was some concern for side effect of this medication.

*Hypothyroidism. Continued on levothyroxine.

*Incidental findings: 
- Well-circumscribed lucent lesion in the distal left clavicle, 
with thin sclerotic rim seen on x-ray. Per radiology read, this 
is non-aggressive in appearance, possible cyst, she had no 
findings of local symptoms. This can be monitored clinically and 
for new symptoms can be followed up with an MRI.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right basilic
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after
establishing intravenous access are on file. A peel-away sheath was then
placed over a guidewire and a double-lumen PICC line measuring 42 cm in length
was then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in the
SVC under fluoroscopic guidance. Position of the catheter was confirmed by a
fluoroscopic spot film of the chest which also shows spinal stimulator device.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed. The catheter was secured
to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

complications.
